_note: Alfred Code 2.1.2 by its README route, non-interactive: the release at tag v2.1.2, pinned by the commit the tag names (f57a70a2 - a tag can move, a commit cannot), fetched ALONE from this repo, one commit deep, and checked out (never a clone: this repo's other branches hold every task's hidden tests, and the plugin source is readable from every cell), so a commit the fetch cannot see fails at that step instead of building HEAD; regenerate arms/ours-vocabulary.txt whenever the pin moves; the official marketplace, then the stack's marketplace added from that source (key envoydev) and the core alfred-code@envoydev installed from it at project scope - BEFORE the installer, which reads the stack's marketplace key off the installed core and would otherwise register the published envoydev/alfred-code; the selection a user gets by taking every recommended option of /alfred-code:setup for the fixture's four stacks (bench/lib/recommended.js, run on the release's own scripts); the installer at project scope, which from 2.1 copies every picked skill into the clone's .claude/skills (the core plugin carries only the /alfred-code router and commands), keeps every agent seat in the core plugin and denies each unpicked one as Agent(alfred-code:<seat>) in the project permissions.deny, and puts the project's data under one root, .alfred (docs at .alfred/docs, the navigation server's state, browser profiles, a project-level memory database; the global memory database sits in the account home's .alfred-memory); then /alfred-code:init, the one-time bootstrap setup's closing card ends on, which runs the captures the install carries (related projects, architecture, code style, the run book, agent capabilities). No capture prompt of its own: setup names init, never a capture, and init refuses to re-run a done one. Onboarding runs with ALFRED_CODE_UNATTENDED=1 (onboardingEnv - the onboarding alone, never a measured cell), the stack's unattended init: nobody answers an ask in print mode, so it takes each question's recommended option and never a destructive one. The template is refused unless init leaves the architecture capture (expects), under the stack's default docs root .alfred/docs, so every cell - the flow block's solve flows included - starts on a captured architecture. B4 checks the selection against a real setup walk.
name: ours
_flow: The flow block's entry per task kind, from the stack's own routing (read at the pin): a feature through the gated single-chat vertical, cross-domain work through its router, and a bug through the diagnoser first - diagnose before coding. From 2.1 each is a project skill copied into the clone's .claude/skills, so its slash name is the bare skill name. The diagnoser never builds: its close names /alfred-task-solve with the findings file it wrote (<docs-path>/diagnoses/<slug>.md, the docs root .alfred/docs), so the second bug prompt sends exactly that, the file resolved in the clone when the prompt is sent.
